# Changelog

## 0.7.1

Retract correction: the 0.7.0 interval missed pseudo-versions.

<details>
<summary>Context</summary>

migrable is retired. 0.7.0 retracted `[v0.0.0, v0.7.0]`, but a closed interval
ending at a release excludes the pseudo-versions the module proxy synthesises
for untagged commits, so `go install github.com/smm-h/migrable@latest` kept
resolving to a pseudo-version built from the branch tip and installing the
retired tool. The interval is now `[v0.0.0-0, v0.7.1]`: `v0.0.0-0` is the
lowest possible pre-release, so every pseudo-version below the upper bound is
inside it, and the upper bound covers this release itself.

This release also corrects the 0.7.0 notes, which claimed the PyPI releases
were yanked. They are not; the yank is still pending and must be done by hand.

Only the go target publishes. Publishing a fresh npm or PyPI artifact would
create a version outside the existing npm deprecation and ahead of the pending
PyPI yank, undoing the retirement this release is meant to complete.

</details>

### Fixes

- **`go install ...@latest` no longer installs the retired tool.** The 0.7.0 retract interval `[v0.0.0, v0.7.0]` excluded pseudo-versions, so `@latest` still resolved to a pseudo-version built from the branch tip. The interval is now `[v0.0.0-0, v0.7.1]`, which starts below every possible pseudo-version and includes this release itself.
- **Corrected a false claim in the 0.7.0 release notes.** They stated the PyPI releases were yanked; they are not. The notes now say the PyPI yank is pending and must be done manually.

## 0.7.0

Retirement release: migrable is superseded by strictspec.

<details>
<summary>Context</summary>

This is the last release migrable will ever make. The project is retired in
favour of strictspec, which covers the same ground.

The release carries the pending work of the 0.6.0 cycle (the strictcli reserved
flag quartet and effect classification, the go-strictcli v0.17.0 BoolFlag
defaults, and the `rlsbl dev install` fix) plus the retirement itself: go.mod
gains a `// Deprecated:` module marker and `retract [v0.0.0, v0.7.0]`, a closed
interval that covers every published version including the proxy-only v0.0.0
and this v0.7.0 release itself. The npm package is deprecated; the PyPI
releases are pending a manual yank. The GitHub repository is archived
afterwards.

Existing consumers with pinned dependencies are unaffected -- retraction is
advisory and does not remove artifacts.

</details>

### Breaking

- **Breaking.** Upgrade go-strictcli to v0.17.0: all BoolFlags now have explicit defaults.
- **Reserved flag names moved to the framework.** `--quiet`, `--verbose` and `--dry-run` are now provided by strictcli on every command instead of being declared by migrable. `--dry-run` is no longer limited to `migrate`, and a dry run additionally prints the framework's `DRY RUN` header. Every command also declares its effect (`init`, `migrate` and `merge` are `mutating`; `status` and `validate` are `read_only`).
- **migrable is retired.** This is the final release; the project is superseded by strictspec. The Go module now carries a `// Deprecated:` marker and retracts every published version, including this one (`retract [v0.0.0, v0.7.0]`), so `go get` and `go install` warn and stop selecting it. The npm package is deprecated; the PyPI releases are pending a manual yank. Existing pinned builds keep working, but no further releases will be made.

### Fixes

- **Fix.** `rlsbl dev install` works again: the go pipeline now declares `install_paths` (the root main package), which newer rlsbl requires for `go install`.

## 0.6.0

### Breaking

- **Breaking.** CLI migrated from Cobra to go-strictcli. `man` command deprecated (use `--help` instead). No other user-facing command changes.
